Starting values for a drmTMB model

Source: R/drmTMBstart.R
drmTMBstart.Rd

Computes starting values for the fixed-effect parameters of a dose-response model, which can be inspected, modified, and passed to the start argument of drmTMB.

Usage

drmTMBstart(
  form,
  fform = NULL,
  data,
  start = NULL,
  fix = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  family = "gaussian",
  model = "logistic",
  alpha = NULL,
  smooth = NULL,
  parlink = NULL,
  curvelink = "identity",
  method = "lm",
  gsl = NULL,
  gsu = NULL,
  gsn = NULL
)

Arguments

form

formula with name of response and dose scale

fform

fixed effects for the model parameters: a formula of the form b2 + b4 ~ Stress, or a list of such formulas, e.g. list(b2 ~ Stress, b4 ~ Stress + Time). Parameters not listed have a single intercept (~ 1). A list of five right-hand side formulas, one for each of b1-b5 (X1 = ~ 1, ..., X5 = ~ 1), is also accepted.

data

a data.frame object. Observations with missing values in the variables of the model or in the weights are left out.

start

starting values, as in drmTMB: named by parameter, e.g. c(b5=0), or one entry for each coefficient. Only NA entries are replaced.

fix

logical, the coefficients fixed at their starting values, as in drmTMB: named by parameter, e.g. c(b5=TRUE), or one entry for each coefficient. Parameters not used by the model are always fixed, at 0 unless given in start, and b1 of event data at 0.

weights

a vector of weights, one for each row of data.

family

the distribution of the response, see drmTMB.

model

the dose-response model, see drmTMB.

alpha

the exponent of the hormesis term of the cedergreen model, see drmTMB.

smooth

smoothing of the threshold of the nec model, relative to the smallest interval between doses, see drmTMB; without random effects, the default is 0, an exact threshold.

parlink

links of the parameters b1-b5, see drmTMB.

curvelink

link of the curve, see drmTMB.

method

"lm" (default), fast starting values from linearised models, or "grid", a grid search of the likelihood, see Details. Random effects are not used; drmTMB starts their standard deviations separately.

gsl

a vector of lower bounds for the grid search, one entry for each model coefficient, on the scale of the coefficients (log scale for b4 with the log link); NA (or NULL) for the default range.

gsu

a vector of upper bounds for the grid search, one entry for each model coefficient; NA (or NULL) for the default range.

gsn

number of grid points for each parameter, a single number or a vector with one entry for each model coefficient (default 10). A parameter with gsn = 1 stays at its "lm" starting value.

Value

a vector of starting values named by the coefficients, as coef of the fit without the variance parameters, including fixed and unused parameters; it can be changed and passed to the argument start of drmTMB.

Details

Method "lm" takes the asymptotes from the mean response at the lowest and highest dose, transforms the response to the relative scale between the asymptotes, and estimates b3 and b4 by linear regression on a linearised version of the model function. The asymmetry parameter b5 starts at 0. Models without such a linearisation use other strategies: for asymptoticregression, exponentialdecay and gamma, b4 is profiled over a grid, with the asymptotes estimated by least squares for each value; for haldane, b4 and the inhibition b5; for nec, thresholds within each interval between the doses; for multistage, the polynomial by least squares; and for exponential and power, the power b3 over a grid. With covariates in fform, the pooled starting value of each parameter is projected onto its design matrix, giving the intercept or each group the pooled value and contrasts a value of zero.

Method "grid" evaluates the negative log-likelihood (without random effects) at all combinations of a grid of parameter values and returns the best grid point; parameters not included in the grid start at the values of method "lm". Without bounds in gsl and gsu, default ranges are used for b3 (the sign of the "lm" starting value, with 1/4 to 4 times its steepness, log-spaced), b4 (the dose range extended at both ends; log-spaced for models on the log-dose scale, and on the log scale with the log link for b4), and b5 (-2 to 2, logistic, loglogistic and nec; for braincousens and cedergreen, from 0 to four times the hormesis effect that equals the difference of the asymptotes at dose b4). Default ranges are only used for parameters with a single coefficient in fform; the asymptotes b1 and b2 are only included in the grid with user-specified bounds.

See also

drmTMB

Examples

# starting values of the log-logistic model, as used by drmTMB
(sv <- drmTMBstart(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic"))
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b4:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>    -0.06896726     8.14026086    -1.71197137     3.74376044     0.00000000 
# changed and passed to drmTMB
sv[c("b1:(Intercept)", "b5:(Intercept)")] <- 0
drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", start = sv,
       fix = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
#> Call:
#> drmTMB(form = rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, start = sv, fix = c(TRUE, 
#>     FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE), model = "loglogistic")
#> 
#> Model:  loglogistic
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for the asymptotes
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> b2:(Intercept)  b3:(Intercept)  b4:(Intercept)  
#>          7.855          -2.470           3.263  
#> Fixed: b1:(Intercept) = 0, b5:(Intercept) = 0
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 0.5616
